First, we need to find the residue of \(9^{2010}\) modulo 17.

We can use properties of modular arithmetic to simplify the problem. Notice that:
\[ 9 \equiv -8 \pmod{17} \]

So, we can rewrite \(9^{2010}\) as:
\[ 9^{2010} \equiv (-8)^{2010} \pmod{17} \]

Next, we need to simplify \((-8)^{2010} \mod 17\). Since 2010 is an even number, we have:
\[ (-8)^{2010} \equiv 64 \pmod{17} \]

Now, we need to find the residue of 64 modulo 17:
\[ 64 \div 17 = 3 \text{ remainder } 13 \]
So,
\[ 64 \equiv 13 \pmod{17} \]

Therefore, the residue of \(9^{2010}\) modulo 17 is \(\boxed{13}\).

We start by generating powers of 9 modulo 17. Note that we can generate $9^{2k}$ from $9^k$ by squaring $9^k$. We get \begin{align*}
9^1 &\equiv 9 \pmod{17} \\
9^2 &\equiv 13 \pmod{17} \\
9^4 &\equiv 16 \pmod{17} \\
9^8 &\equiv 1 \pmod{17}.
\end{align*}Since $9^8 \equiv 1$ modulo 17, we have \begin{align*}
9^{2010} &\equiv 9^2 9^{2008} \\
&\equiv 9^2 (9^8)^{251} \\
&\equiv 9^2 1^{251} \\
&\equiv 9^2 \\
&\equiv \boxed{13} \pmod{17}.
\end{align*}
